rules.title: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version)
rules.requirement: Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property not exempt; increases on or after 2019-03-15; section repealed 2030-01-01
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school dormitories; housing under local rent control that limits increases below this cap; certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable unit (single-family home or condo) of a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory notice; owner-occupied duplex; mobilehome homeowners
rules.interaction: Yields to local rent control that restricts increases below the state cap (subd. (d)(3)): LA RSO, San Francisco, Berkeley, Santa Ana; San Diego has no local cap. Section operative 2024-04-01 per subd. (n) (SB 567, effective 2024-01-01). D040 (LAHD JCO page) restates the same cap and was merged here.
rules.quoted_span: shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

all.unavailable: unit alienable separately (single-family home or condo) owned by a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory exemption notice
owner occupied one of the two units as principal residence since the start of the tenancy, neither unit an ADU

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies after 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (24 months if adult tenants were added); section repealed 2030-01-01
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, care facilities; school dormitories; tenant sharing bath or kitchen with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family home renting up to two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable unit of a non-REIT, non-corporate owner with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; property covered by a qualifying local just cause ordinance
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later more protective one, covers the property (subd. (i)); yields to the LA, San Diego, Santa Ana, San Francisco and Berkeley just cause rules. Section operative 2024-04-01 per subd. (m); current text amended by AB 1529, effective 2026-01-01.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause

all.unavailable: single-family owner-occupied residence renting no more than two units or bedrooms
owner occupied one of the two units as principal residence since the start of the tenancy, neither unit an ADU
unit alienable separately (single-family home or condo) owned by a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory exemption notice

rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for residential rental agreements collected or demanded on or after 2024-07-01
rules.exemptions: Not an exemption but a variant: a landlord who is a natural person (or LLC of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may take up to two months' rent, except from a service member; advance payment of six months' rent or more allowed for leases of six months or longer
rules.interaction: Statewide; no local deposit cap found for the CA1 cities. The cap applies to security collected on or after 2024-07-01 per subd. (c)(6); the section was last amended by AB 414 (effective 2026-01-01, photo and return rules). LA RSO units also earn deposit interest under L.A.M.C. 151.06.02.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent

rules.title: Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents charging applicants (including guarantors and cosigners) to screen residential rental applications
rules.interaction: Statewide; the fee is not security under 1950.5. The text gives no current CPI-adjusted dollar figure and no single official 2026 figure exists (starter README section 9). effective_date is the AB 1170 amendment (2026-01-01); the $30 cap itself is older.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267)
rules.requirement: Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered.
rules.key_value: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations and others in real estate transactions in California
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupant renting to one additional person may choose among applicants (but may not publish discriminatory statements); senior housing may limit by age
rules.interaction: Statewide floor; LA (L.A.M.C. 45.65 to 45.69) and San Diego (S.D.M.C. 98.0801 to 98.0806) add local source-of-income rules. effective_date 2020-01-01 is when SB 329 made vouchers part of source of income (X021, secondary; the brief names this cell 'FEHA (SB 329)'); the current text, incl. the credit-history alternative, is the SB 267 amendment effective 2024-01-01 (D027). Criminal-history limits come from CRD guidance (D016) that cites no section, so they are folded in here.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income

all.unavailable: owner occupies the home and rents to only one additional person

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in California; not rental-specific
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not covered persons
rules.interaction: Effective date evidence: D022 shows AB 325 chaptered 2025-10-06 (Ch. 338) and its text gives no effective date; 2026-01-01 comes from organizer test T1 (data/dev/change_tests.json), the Cleary Gottlieb alert X024 and the brief (1/1/2026). Statewide antitrust rule that sits alongside the local bans in San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley and Santa Ana.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

all.unavailable: owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease without one of the good causes listed in the Act, and must prove that cause in court. Most causes require a written Notice to Quit, and some a Notice to Cease first.
rules.key_value: Good cause required for eviction or non-renewal (statutory grounds); Notice to Quit for all causes except nonpayment
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, apartment buildings and complexes, mobile homes, rooming and boarding homes
rules.exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient or seasonal hotel, motel or guest house guests; unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a
rules.interaction: Statewide; applies alongside local rent control in Jersey City, Hoboken and Newark. Quote from the supplied DCA guide (D067); statute text X011 (supplemental) confirms the grounds and the owner-occupied two-rental-unit exception but gives no effective date for the current version.

all.unavailable: owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units and the tenant has not invoked the law by 30 days written notice

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: A landlord may not take a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent, and a yearly top-up may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. The deposit must be held in a New Jersey interest-bearing account, interest belongs to the tenant, and it must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26)
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units), unless the tenant gives 30 days written notice invoking the law; interest-account rules do not apply to seasonal rentals of 125 days or less
rules.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
rules.interaction: Statewide. Quote from the supplied DCA guide (D067); statute texts X012 (46:8-21.2, cap and 10% rule, history 'amended 2003, c.188', a year not an effective date) and X013 (46:8-26, coverage section of the same act) merged into this one record.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to rent a home; the cap is adjusted each January 1 by CPI. Violations carry penalties and the overcharge is returned to the applicant.
rules.key_value: $50 cap, CPI-adjusted yearly
rules.coverage_conditions: Application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes
rules.exemptions: Dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling; a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord
rules.quoted_span: shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.interaction: Statewide (C.46:8-18.1). Effective date computed from section 3 (first day of the fourth month after approval on January 20, 2026), matching the brief (eff. 5/1/2026). The licensee carve-out concerns who charges the fee, not the building, so it is not in exempt_if.

all.unavailable: owner occupies the other unit of a two-family dwelling, or rents rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent or treat an applicant differently because of the source of lawful income or rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher. A landlord may still refuse for insufficient income or poor credit.
rules.key_value: Source of lawful income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected basis
rules.coverage_conditions: Sale or rental of all real property, residential or business
rules.exemptions: Single apartment in a two-family dwelling whose other unit the owner occupies; rooms rented in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preference; housing for older persons (familial status only)
rules.quoted_span: a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
rules.interaction: Separate instrument from the Fair Chance in Housing Act in the same cell. Quote from the DCR brochure (D068); the cite N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h) is printed in the DCA guide (D067), which also lists source of lawful income as protected. Neither text gives an effective date.

all.unavailable: owner-occupied premises

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about criminal history on an application or before making a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, must do an individualized assessment, and must give written reasons if they withdraw the offer.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before a conditional offer; lookback 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree), 1 year (4th degree); penalties up to $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers offering a rental dwelling unit for residential purposes
rules.exemptions: Dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.quoted_span: shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.interaction: Statewide (C.46:8-52 et seq.); the text contains no preemption clause, so it applies alongside Newark's ban-the-box ordinance. Effective date computed from section 14 (first day of the seventh month after approval on June 18, 2021).

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: From July 1, 2027, landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's rent-setting service that pools competitors' nonpublic data or sets rents, lease terms or occupancy by algorithm, and no one may perform that coordinating function. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic coordination of rents, lease terms or occupancy using competitors' nonpublic data; effective 2027-07-01
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental property owners, coordinators and their agents; any residential dwelling unit used as a primary residence in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Inpatient medical, long-term care and detention facilities are not dwelling units; research or testing use; free public rent estimates; equal-terms brokerage listing databases; government affordability controls; non-AI spreadsheets needing human analysis and plain database queries
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.interaction: Possible preemption of the Jersey City and Hoboken bans, for human review: section 6.b reads "A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act." and adds that it does not bar ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law; it does not say whether ordinances enacted before the act are void. Approved July 20, 2026; effective date computed from section 9 (first day of the twelfth month after enactment), matching the brief, T3 and X025.

rules.coverage_conditions: Every Massachusetts city and town
rules.exemptions: Narrow exception for a town that accepts c.40P: voluntary-only regulation, not for owners of fewer than ten units or units with fair market rent above $400, owners compensated by the town
rules.interaction: Bars local rent control in Boston and Cambridge; statute text carries no effective date. The 2026 ballot question to repeal it (IP 25-21) was struck, see MA-02.
rules.title: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap.
rules.key_value: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

rules.coverage_conditions: Would have covered most residential rental units statewide
rules.exemptions: Proposed: owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain regulated units, short-term rentals, educational, religious or nonprofit facilities
rules.interaction: Supplemental source (no supplied D doc covers it; D059 was link-only): X023 for the petition number and terms, X007 (WBUR, 2026-06-23) and organizer test T5 for the struck status. Evidence that no rent cap applies in Boston or Cambridge; M.G.L. c.40P s.4 stays in force.
rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases (struck from 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: A 2026 ballot question would have repealed the c.40P ban and capped annual rent increases. The Supreme Judicial Court removed it from the November 2026 ballot on 2026-06-23 (Cella v. Attorney General), so it is not law and no rent cap applies.
rules.key_value: Failed: proposed cap of the lesser of CPI or 5% never took effect
rules.quoted_span: The case, Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (embedded below), involved Initiative Petition 25-21

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential leases and tenancies
rules.exemptions: Leases or tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
rules.interaction: Statewide; no Boston or Cambridge deposit rule found. Effective date is the 2025 c.9 amendment of clause (1)(b) (adds lessor's agents, fee in lieu of deposit capped with the deposit at 1 month's rent); the one-month cap itself is older.
rules.title: Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B)
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3)

rules.coverage_conditions: Licensed brokers or salespersons finding rental housing for a fee
rules.interaction: Statute text marks this version as amended by 2025 c.9 s.43, effective August 1, 2025. Separate instrument from the c.186 s.15B upfront-charge limit (MA-04).
rules.title: Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2)
rules.requirement: A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.coverage_conditions: Lessors and agents of the lessor, at or before the start of a residential tenancy
rules.exemptions: Leases or tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
rules.interaction: Same statute as the deposit rule (MA-03), recorded here for the upfront-charge limit; X022 (secondary) confirms landlords may not charge application fees. Current text of clause (1)(b) effective 2025-08-01 (2025 c.9). Broker fees are governed separately by M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (MA-05).
rules.title: Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed.
rules.key_value: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.coverage_conditions: Any person furnishing rental accommodations
rules.interaction: Statewide floor; Boston and Cambridge add local source-of-income protections. No effective date in the text. Criminal-record screening is recorded separately under 803 CMR 5.00 (MA-12).
rules.title: Source of income and housing subsidy discrimination (M.G.L. c.151B s.4(10))
rules.requirement: A landlord may not discriminate against an applicant or tenant because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a Section 8 voucher, or because of the requirements of that program.
rules.key_value: No refusal based on public assistance or housing subsidy (vouchers)
rules.quoted_span: or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient

rules.title: Criminal record (CORI) checks for housing applicants (803 CMR 5.00)
rules.requirement: A landlord, property manager or real estate agent may request a standard criminal record (CORI) check only on the housing applicant and only as the final step of the application, and may not use it to screen other household members.
rules.key_value: CORI only as the final step of the application; applicant only
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords, property management companies and real estate agents evaluating applicants for market rate housing
rules.quoted_span: CORI shall only be requested for a housing applicant as the final step in the application process.
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: X029 (Cornell LII mirror of 803 CMR 5.04) because the supplied doc D056 was link-only (403). Effective date is the latest amendment shown (Mass Register Issue 1445, eff. 6/11/2021). Subsidized and public housing rules (5.05 and later) not read.
Organizer test T4 (MA-ALG-P1/P2): pending, never in force; would cover all MA addresses if enacted. Bill text not in the corpus.
rules.title: H.5222, An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market (194th General Court)
rules.requirement: Pending House bill to prevent algorithmic rent fixing; reported favorably by the Housing committee on 3/12/2026 (new draft of H.1564) and referred to House Ways and Means. It is not law.
rules.key_value: Pending: would prevent algorithmic rent fixing
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.interaction: Organizer test T4 (MA-ALG-P1/P2): pending, never in force; would cover all MA addresses if enacted. Bill text not in the corpus, so coverage and penalties unknown. D047 is the same bill history.
rules.title: S.2983, An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (194th General Court)
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill to prohibit algorithmic rent setting; reported favorably by the Housing committee on 3/12/2026 and referred to Senate Ways and Means. It is not law.
rules.key_value: Pending: would prohibit algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase
rules.requirement: In RSO units rent may be raised once every 12 months by the annual allowable percentage published by LAHD (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Since the formula change no extra percentage for utilities or for an added dependent is allowed; rent resets to market only after a vacancy such as a voluntary move-out or buyout.
rules.key_value: LAHD annual allowable %, once per 12 months (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30); no utility or dependent add-on
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before 1978-10-01 plus replacement units under L.A.M.C. 151.28: apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, ADUs, rooms rented over 30 days, mobile homes; condos and townhomes only for tenancies begun on or before 1995-12-31
rules.exemptions: Single-family dwelling alone on its parcel; condo or townhome tenancies begun after 1995-12-31 (rent not regulated); luxury exemption (by application, rent level on or before 1978-05-31); temporary exemptions on registration
rules.interaction: Takes precedence over the state cap Civ. Code 1947.12 for covered units. The rate page D042 shows 3% only through 2026-06-30; the 2026-27 percentage is not in the corpus. Non-RSO units fall under the state cap and the JCO.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates for the new RSO formula: 2026-02-02 per LAHD (D041, D042, official, kept) and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association (reported in docs/starter_README.md section 9; that source is not in the corpus). Human review needed.

all.unavailable: single-family dwelling that is the only dwelling on its parcel
condominium or townhome tenancy commenced after 1995-12-31

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units
rules.requirement: A landlord may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault reason (non-payment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew, denying access, unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reason (owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the market, government order, conversion), and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions ($11,000 to $27,400 per unit for 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30).
rules.key_value: just cause required; no-fault relocation $11,000 to $27,400 (2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30)
rules.coverage_conditions: JCO: most rental units not regulated by the RSO (buildings newer than 1978-10-01, a lone single-family dwelling), once the tenant has lived there six months or the original lease expired. RSO units (built on or before 1978-10-01) get the same just cause list under L.A.M.C. 151.09.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, some cooperatives, some nonprofit homeless or treatment facilities, some HACLA or government property
rules.interaction: Two LA instruments share this cell: the JCO (L.A.M.C. 165.00 et seq., non-RSO units, primary here) and the RSO eviction section L.A.M.C. 151.09 (RSO units, D041); both use the same causes and the same relocation chart (D043, Bulletin A), so one record covers every LA rental. Replaces state Civ. Code 1946.2 for covered property. JCO effective date not stated in the corpus.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits, monthly or yearly, as a direct payment or rent credit, and tell the tenant in writing which method they use. The City sets the rate each year.
rules.key_value: annual interest on RSO security deposits (rate set yearly by LAHD)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Los Angeles RSO (first built on or before 1978-10-01)
rules.interaction: Adds to, and does not replace, the state deposit cap Civ. Code 1950.5. D041 (LAHD) lists deposit interest among RSO requirements; the section number, payment rules and rates come from the AAGLA page X020 (secondary, supplemental source), which quotes interest accruing from 1990-11-01 (an accrual start, not the effective date of the current section, so effective_date stays null; latest rate shown there is 4.320% for 2025). No LA deposit cap found.
rules.quoted_span: Interest Payments on Security Deposits

rules.title: Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination
rules.requirement: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction.
rules.key_value: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance)
rules.coverage_conditions: All housing accommodations in the City of Los Angeles rented or offered for rent
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: no supplied D doc covers this ordinance (D038 is link-only), so X017 (codified text, sec. 45.69 effective 2020-01-01) is quoted and earns no citation credit. Adds to state FEHA (Gov. Code 12955). No LA criminal-history screening ordinance found in D040, D041, D043 or X017.
rules.quoted_span: Based upon a person’s source of income, refuse to rent or lease, or to continue to rent or lease, a housing accommodation;

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance)
rules.requirement: In rent-controlled units, the landlord may raise the rent once a year by the Rent Board's annual allowable increase: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 (1.4% the year before). Units that first got a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from these rent limits.
rules.key_value: annual allowable increase 1.6% (3/1/2026 to 2/28/2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units with a certificate of occupancy on or before June 13, 1979
rules.exemptions: Units that first obtained a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency
rules.interaction: Local rent control; the California statewide cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12) yields to it where it covers the unit. Rate confirmed by D083; the June 13, 1979 certificate-of-occupancy cutoff is stated in D079 and the brief.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (Section 37.9)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just causes, and it must be the dominant motive; lease expiry or a change of owner is not a just cause. No-fault evictions such as owner move-in trigger relocation payments.
rules.key_value: 17 just causes; relocation $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly, disabled or minor-child household (owner move-in and similar, notices served 3/1/2026 to 2/28/2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including post-June 13, 1979 new construction and Costa-Hawkins tenancies that are exempt only from the rent limits
rules.exemptions: Some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency (source gives no full list)
rules.interaction: Local just cause rule; the California statewide just cause rule (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2) yields to it. Relocation amounts (Section 37.9C, Ellis Act amounts in 37.9A) from D082 and D083.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest rate
rules.requirement: The San Francisco Rent Board publishes an annual interest rate that applies to tenant security deposits: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 (5.0% the year before). The source lists the rate but not the ordinance or its coverage.
rules.key_value: 4.2% security deposit interest (3/1/2026 to 2/28/2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Not stated in the source
rules.interaction: Adds an interest rate on deposits; the deposit cap itself is state law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5). Official code cite not in any supplied or gap-fill text.
rules.citation: S.F. Rent Board security deposit interest rate
rules.quoted_span: Security Deposit Interest: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, housing provisions (Police Code § 4906)
rules.requirement: For affordable housing, a housing provider may not ask about or use arrests without conviction, dismissed or expunged convictions, juvenile matters, convictions more than seven years old, infractions or decriminalized conduct, and may ask about conviction history only after finding the applicant eligible and qualified. Decisions need an individualized assessment, and the applicant gets 14 days to respond to a notice of adverse action.
rules.key_value: affordable housing only: no inquiry before eligibility check; 7-year look-back limit; individualized assessment; 14 days to respond to a notice of adverse action
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers, regarding applicants and household members for Affordable Housing (defined in § 4903, not in the corpus)
rules.interaction: Adds to state fair housing rules (Cal. Gov. Code § 12955). Quote from supplied D078, which names the ordinance only; X031 (city code library, supplemental source) supplies the official cite, the requirements and the dates (added by Ord. 17-14, operative 8/13/2014; last amended by Ord. 128-26, effective 8/10/2026).
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

applies_if.unavailable: affordable housing (the ordinance covers affordable housing decisions)

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: No one may sell or use an algorithmic device that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney can sue.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor rental data
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco
rules.interaction: Applies alongside the California statewide rules on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763)). X018 (law-firm alert) agrees on October 2024 and adds penalties up to $1,000 per violation per unit and month.
rules.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Tenant Protection Ordinance), just cause and relocation
rules.requirement: A landlord may not end a tenancy without an at-fault or no-fault just cause. For a no-fault termination the landlord must pay two months' rent (three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled), or waive that much rent, regardless of income or tenancy length.
rules.key_value: just cause required; no-fault relocation 2 months' rent (3 months for senior or disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property with tenancies over 30 days, from the start of the tenancy
rules.exemptions: Hotels and short-term rentals; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); mobilehomes under the MRL; nonprofit hospital, care and transitional housing; dormitories; tenant sharing bath or kitchen with resident landlord; landlord-occupied single-family home; landlord-occupied duplex; certificate of occupancy within 15 years; separately alienable unit of a non-REIT, non-corporate landlord with notice
rules.interaction: Local just cause consistent with Civ. Code 1946.2, which yields to it (98.0701). Current division added by O-21647 N.S. (effective 2023-06-24) and amended by O-21769 N.S. (effective 2024-03-28); the LASSD FAQ X027 agrees.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.

all.unavailable: single-family residence occupied by the landlord as principal residence
owner occupied one of the two units as principal residence since the start of the tenancy, neither unit an ADU
unit alienable separately (single-family home or condo) owned by a non-REIT, non-corporate owner who gave the statutory exemption notice

rules.title: San Diego prohibition of source-of-income discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or renew, end a tenancy, or set different terms because of a person's source of income, including any rental assistance, vouchers or subsidy, and income standards must count all of a tenant's income and the combined income of co-tenants and cosigners.
rules.key_value: no refusal or different terms based on source of income, incl. any rental assistance
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units and tenancies in the City of San Diego
rules.exemptions: Tenancies where the owner or a family member lives in the same building and shares a bathroom or kitchen with the tenant
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: no supplied D doc carries this division (D075 is link-only and the X016 capture was an empty page), so X028 (official codified text, added by O-20986 N.S., effective 2018-10-18) is quoted and earns no citation credit. Broadens state FEHA source-of-income protection.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for any person to do any of the following acts, wholly or in part, based on a person’s source of income

rules.title: San Diego Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing (Division 11)
rules.requirement: No one may sell, license or provide to a landlord, and no landlord may use, software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to recommend rents or occupancy levels. A tenant can sue for an injunction, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego and sellers of such software
rules.exemptions: Reports from public data or aggregated data over 90 days old that do not recommend future rents; affordable-housing program rent or income limit tools; appraisal software that does not recommend rents
rules.interaction: Content quoted from the supplied draft ordinance D076 (O-2025-107, passage date blank); status and date from the codified text X015 (added 5-22-2025 by O-21955 N.S., effective 2025-06-21), confirmed by the brief and X018. The enacted remedies section makes fee shifting two-way. Coexists with state Bus. & Prof. Code 16729.
rules.quoted_span: (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance (rent ceilings)
rules.requirement: In fully covered units, the landlord may raise the rent ceiling once a year by the Annual General Adjustment: 1.0% for 2026, no earlier than January 1, 2026. The adjustment is 65% of CPI and, since Measure BB, at most 5%.
rules.key_value: 2026 AGA 1.0% (65% of CPI, max 5%)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses (5 or more rooms rented separately). Partially covered (no rent ceiling): new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980 (D009; D006 says after 1980), most condominiums, later single-family tenancies, some subsidized units
rules.exemptions: Golden duplex; owner shares kitchen or bath and lived there first; ADU property with owner occupancy (tenancies after Nov 7, 2018); university housing; nonprofit cooperatives; condominiums and Section 202, Section 811 or HUD-insured subsidy units are only partially covered (no rent ceiling). The 2026 AGA does not apply to Costa-Hawkins tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025
rules.interaction: Local rent control; the California statewide cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12) yields to it where it covers the unit. Coverage from D006 and D009, 5% cap from D006 (Measure BB), formula cite BMC 13.76.110A from D008.
rules.quoted_span: eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than

all.unavailable: golden duplex: duplex owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and currently with an owner living in one of the units
tenancy started after Nov 7, 2018 on a property where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance (just cause)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units can be evicted only for just cause. Since Measure BB, no eviction for rent debt below one month of Fair Market Rent or for refusing a new fixed-term lease, and notices must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days.
rules.key_value: just cause required; no nonpayment eviction below one month's Fair Market Rent; owner move-in and Ellis relocation $19,413 plus $6,471 for qualifying households (from 1/1/2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance (includes new construction, condominiums and single-family homes)
rules.exemptions: Golden duplex; owner shares kitchen or bath and lived there first; ADU property with owner occupancy (tenancies after Nov 7, 2018); university housing; nonprofit cooperatives
rules.interaction: Local just cause rule; the California statewide just cause rule (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2) yields to it. Coverage from D009, relocation amounts from D004.
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).

all.unavailable: golden duplex: duplex owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and currently with an owner living in one of the units
tenancy started after Nov 7, 2018 on a property where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest (Rent Ordinance)
rules.requirement: Landlords of units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on the security deposit every year, and a prorated amount when the tenant moves out.
rules.key_value: annual interest on security deposits
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.exemptions: Exempt unit types under the Rent Ordinance (golden duplex, shared kitchen or bath, owner-occupied ADU property, university housing, nonprofit cooperatives)
rules.interaction: The deposit cap (one month, two for qualifying small landlords, from July 1, 2024) is state law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5, AB 12), not local; D009 confirms deposit interest applies to fully and partially covered units.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

all.unavailable: golden duplex: duplex owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and currently with an owner living in one of the units
tenancy started after Nov 7, 2018 on a property where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening and application fee ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord who charges a screening fee must first give a tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee. Landlords may not charge existing tenants non-refundable fees to renew a tenancy or to add, replace or remove a roommate.
rules.key_value: fee-rights statement required; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants (state cap $68.96 in 2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, regardless of lease terms
rules.interaction: Adds disclosure and existing-tenant fee limits on top of the state screening-fee cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6), which sets the dollar amount.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before acting on it. Fines run from $1,000 to $10,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in rental decisions; fines $1,000 to $10,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, current and prospective tenants
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied properties with 1 to 3 units where an owner of record lives; lifetime sex offenders; limited public housing and Section 8 exemptions; owner move-back units under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding roommates
rules.interaction: Adds to state fair housing rules (Cal. Gov. Code § 12955). Passed April 14, 2020 per D003; no effective date stated.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

all.unavailable: an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

rules.title: Berkeley prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms (Ordinance 7,992-N.S.)
rules.requirement: No one may sell or provide, and no landlord may use, a coordinated pricing algorithm that uses nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy for Berkeley units. The City Attorney or a tenant can sue; penalties up to $1,000 per violation, each unit and month counted separately.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential dwelling units in Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Aggregated anonymous reports that do not recommend rents; affordable-housing rent or income limit tools; market research for project financing, appraisals, software research and training
rules.interaction: Applies alongside the California statewide rules (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763)). X018 also reports RealPage v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: March 1, 2026 in the ordinance text (participant guide section 9) and January 2026 per an August 2026 Morgan Lewis alert (X018). The supplied ordinance copy (D001, passed to print November 18, 2025) states no date. Both dates are before 2026-10-01, so the ban is in force either way.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases may not exceed the lower of 3% or 80% of the 12-month CPI change, and none is allowed if CPI is negative; the maximum for 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31 is 2.87%. Owners may petition for more to get a fair return.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Santa Ana
rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after 1995-02-01; mobile home spaces first offered for rent after 1990-01-01
rules.interaction: Local rent stabilization stricter than Civ. Code 1947.12, which yields to it. Effective 2021-11-19 per the city adoption notice D085; formula and current rate per D084. Municipal code section numbers are not in the corpus.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: 2.87 percent is the maximum allowable rent increase for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.

all.unavailable: building constructed after February 1, 1995

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy an owner may end a tenancy only for a just cause stated in writing, after first giving notice and time to fix a violation. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay 3 months of relocation assistance or waive the final 3 months of rent.
rules.key_value: just cause after 30 days; no-fault relocation 3 months' rent or rent waiver
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Santa Ana, after the first 30 days of tenancy
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotels and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters
rules.interaction: Local just cause; Civ. Code 1946.2 yields to it. D084 confirms the program is current (2026). Municipal code section numbers are not in the corpus.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software (Ordinance NS-3090)
rules.requirement: No one may sell, license or provide, and no landlord may use, rent-setting software that relies on nonpublic competitor data for Santa Ana residential rentals. Tenants can sue for an injunction, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (per month) plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits
rules.exemptions: Pricing software relying solely on public or aggregate historical data; tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: no supplied D doc covers it (D086 and D087 are link-only), so the Morgan Lewis alert X018 is quoted (no citation credit). Adoption: first reading 2026-02-17, final vote 2026-03-03 (X009, X008); 2026-04-02 is consistent with the brief's April 2026. Official ordinance text is not in the corpus. Coexists with state Bus. & Prof. Code 16729.
rules.quoted_span: Santa Ana Ordinance No. NS-3090 (effective April 2, 2026)

all.unavailable: exemption granted on a Rent Control Exemption Request (e.g. newly constructed multiple dwelling, N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5)

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rent increases in Jersey City buildings with 5 or more units are regulated by the Rent Control Ordinance and its Rent Leveling Board; all 1 to 4 unit properties are exempt. Owners may ask the Office of Landlord Tenant Relations for other permitted exemptions.
rules.key_value: Rent control for buildings of 5 or more units (1 to 4 unit properties exempt); cap formula not stated in the source (city links a CPI chart)
rules.coverage_conditions: Properties with 5 or more units
rules.exemptions: All 1 to 4 unit properties; other permitted exemptions granted on a Rent Control Exemption Request; newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years after completion under state law (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5, per D067); some government-subsidized rents
rules.quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)
rules.interaction: Local rent control; NJ has no state rent cap (D067). The state new-construction exemption is encoded as building age under 30 plus an unavailable grant fact; subsidized-housing exemptions are listed only in text. Missing units or year_built give unknown.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords and their agents may not subscribe to, contract with or pay a service provider that collects nonpublic competitor information and uses an algorithm to recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy levels, and service providers may not facilitate agreements not to compete. Enforcement is public and private; repeat violations are fined $100 to $2,000, each day a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on paying for algorithmic rent-coordination services; repeat violations $100 to $2,000 per day
rules.coverage_conditions: Real estate lessors, their agents and subcontractors, and service providers, for residential dwelling units in Jersey City
rules.exemptions: Owners of multiple properties for actions related exclusively to properties they control; licensed real estate agents acting in accordance with state rules
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: official text of Ord. 25-057 (X030, adopted May 21 2025, mayor approved May 22 2025), which prints no effective date; 2025-06 from the law-firm alert X018 and the brief (Jun 2025). No supplied D doc covers the ban. Possible preemption by the NJ FAIR Act, P.L.2026, c.43, from 2027-07-01 (human review via conflicts_with).

any.unavailable: coverage under section 155-2 (not captured), building vacant since January 1, 1984, or unit decontrolled under art. VII or VIII

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: At lease renewal a landlord of a rent-controlled Hoboken unit may not raise the rent by more than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less, and only once in 12 months, with 30 days written notice explaining the reason. Tax, water/sewer and capital improvement surcharges need separate approval.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 5% or CPI change per year
rules.coverage_conditions: Dwellings to which Hoboken Code ch. 155 applies (coverage section 155-2 not in the captured text)
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, on determination by the Rent Regulation Officer; vacancy decontrol (art. VII) and condo/co-op initial rental decontrol (art. VIII); criteria not in the captured text
rules.quoted_span: no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: Hoboken ecode pages (X001 to X003) have no supplied D-doc equivalent. effective_date is the adoption date of Ord. B-532 (2-1-2023), the history tag over section 155-5 (cap); chapter adopted 1-16-1984 (X001). Coverage and exemption criteria are not captured, so the exemption stays unknown for every address.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on price fixing using algorithmic pricing
rules.requirement: Landlords of any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. Violations go to Hoboken Municipal Court.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic pricing using nonpublic competitor data (under 365 days old); fine up to $2,000 or up to 90 days community service
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential dwelling unit used as a primary residence in Hoboken
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.interaction: Supplemental source (codified text X003, adopted 7-9-2025 by Ord. B-781; X018 and the brief say effective July 2025, consistent). Possible preemption by the NJ FAIR Act from 2027-07-01 (human review via conflicts_with).

all.unavailable: Rent Control Board certification of newly constructed multiple dwelling exemption (19:2-18.1)

rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: At lease renewal a Newark landlord may not raise rent by more than the CPI-U change over the prior 15 to 3 months, and never more than 4%, once per 12 months, with 30 days written notice. No increase is allowed if the dwelling is not in substantial code compliance or not registered.
rules.key_value: CPI-U change, max 4% per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings in Newark (any building with one or more apartments rented or offered for rent)
rules.exemptions: Public housing; transient hotel/motel space; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings certified by the Rent Control Board, for 30 years after completion or the initial mortgage amortization period if shorter (19:2-18.1); substantially rehabilitated vacant dwellings for 5 years (19:2-18.2); Rental Rehabilitation Program units with Section 8; units under a government rent-regulation contract
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.interaction: Supplemental source (Newark ecode X004, no supplied D-doc equivalent). effective_date is the adoption date of Ord. 6PSF-I that last amended section 19:2-3. Only the new-construction exemption is encoded (age under 30 plus unavailable certification); program and use-type exemptions are listed in text.

all.unavailable: owner occupies the other unit of a two-family dwelling, or rents rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling

rules.title: Newark Ban the Box housing ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords and brokers may check criminal history only after a formal application, with notice and consent, and may look back only 8 years for indictable convictions or 5 years for disorderly persons offenses (plus listed serious offenses and pending charges). Arrests without conviction, expunged and juvenile records may not be used, and denials need written reasons.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiry only after a formal application; 8-year / 5-year lookback; fines up to $500 first, $1,000 repeat
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental, lease or sublease of real property by a landlord or real estate broker in Newark
rules.exemptions: Single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; where federal or state law requires or permits criminal history consideration; property in a government program housing people with criminal histories
rules.quoted_span: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.
rules.interaction: Supplemental source (Newark ecode X006). Applies alongside the state Fair Chance in Housing Act (no preemption clause in either text). effective_date is the adoption date of Ord. 6 PSF-B.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7)
rules.requirement: Any Boston landlord ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the notice to quit or notice of non-renewal, and send a copy of the notice to the city. Fines can reach $300 per day.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with every notice to quit or non-renewal
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or occupancy in Boston
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.
rules.interaction: Notice-of-rights rule (the category covers notice); it does not limit the grounds for eviction, and Massachusetts has no just-cause statute. Effective 2020-11-06 per the city FAQ (D014).

rules.coverage_conditions: Renting, buying, selling or financing housing in the City of Boston
rules.interaction: City web summary that names no ordinance section or date; enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission alongside M.G.L. c.151B s.4(10).
rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations: rental assistance as a protected class

rules.key_value: No discrimination based on rental assistance (Section 8 and other vouchers)

rules.title: Tenants' Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 8.71)
rules.requirement: Cambridge landlords must give tenants the city's tenant rights and resources guide at the start of a tenancy and when taking steps to end it (notice to quit or summary process). Fines can reach $300 per day.
rules.key_value: Rights and resources guide at lease start and with notice to quit
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single units
rules.exemptions: Hospital, skilled nursing or health facility units, non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities, short-term rental units

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source of income protection
rules.requirement: Cambridge landlords may not discriminate against renters based on source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8, public benefits) protected

no_rule.note: San Diego's tenant protection division has no rent cap, and the notice it requires landlords to give (S.D.M.C. 98.0705) sends tenants to state Civ. Code 1947.12 for rent limits, while it says 'Local law also provides' only for just cause. X027 (LASSD FAQ) repeats this notice. So state 1947.12 governs San Diego rents.

D039 is a 2024-09-03 council motion that only asks LAHD to report on feasibility of a ban. The Morgan Lewis survey of local algorithmic rent laws dated 2026-08-21 (X018) lists San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley and Santa Ana but not Los Angeles, and the brief's examples omit LA. State Bus. & Prof. Code 16729 still applies.

The brief's illustrative San Francisco lookup cites only Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 for the screening fee while layering local rules in the rent, just cause and algorithmic rows; no supplied SF doc (D078 to D083) names a local fee rule. Medium confidence: no SF text positively says there is none.

Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction statute: c.186 s.12 (D051) lets either party end a tenancy at will by written notice without cause; c.186 s.11 and s.31 (D050, D058) are notice-to-quit rules for nonpayment and s.18 (D053) is anti-retaliation, none limits the grounds for eviction.

M.G.L. c.40P s.4 bars local rent control; H.3744 (D011, 193rd General Court), a home-rule petition to let Boston adopt rent stabilization, never passed (accompanied a study order 9/9/2024); IP 25-21 struck (T5).
Deposits are governed by state law M.G.L. c.186 s.15B (D052); no Boston deposit ordinance in the Boston sources (D010 to D014). Inferred, not stated by a Boston document.
M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b) (D052) limits all upfront charges statewide and c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (D057) governs broker fees; no Boston fee ordinance in D010 to D014. Inferred.
No Boston algorithmic rent-setting ordinance in any source; the only Massachusetts measures are the pending state bills S.2983 and H.5222 (D046, D045). Inferred.
M.G.L. c.40P s.4 bars local rent control in Cambridge; IP 25-21 struck (T5), so no rent cap.
Deposits governed by state law M.G.L. c.186 s.15B (D052); no Cambridge deposit ordinance in D029 or D031. Inferred.
Upfront charges limited statewide by M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b) (D052), broker fees by c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (D057); no Cambridge fee ordinance in D029 or D031. Inferred.

Cambridge Day (X026, supplied link D030) reports only a council policy order asking the city manager to draft policy options or ordinance language; no ordinance enacted or filed. State bills S.2983/H.5222 pending.
DCA Truth in Renting guide: 'The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.' Rent control is municipal (Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark records).

Organizer test T2 and the brief: the Hoboken and Jersey City bans apply only in their own cities, 'neither for Newark'; no Newark ordinance in X004 to X006. Statewide FAIR Act (NJ-06) covers Newark from 2027-07-01.
